summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update14.json → valid=true; re-declaring the two previously registered source ids was accepted). Closed the source-decidable half of the vote-record question and sharpened its mechanism, as a successor interpretation plus a new Fact. (1) Atomicity within the captured tree is settled: the vote term and the encoded candidate identity are two named keys (raft.go:27-29) written only by persistVote as two single-key operations (2130-2138) over an interface with no batch primitive, and no other code path writes either key — so the pair is never atomic in this codebase, leaving only store-level behaviour and severity open. (2) The write order is load-bearing: with the term written and the candidate not, the residue reads as 'newer term, the previous term's candidate', which the duplicate branch answers by identity comparison and grants without the log up-to-dateness check (1697-1705); the opposite order would have produced 'older term, this term's candidate', which the branch answers by refusing another identity at that term — a lost re-vote rather than an unchecked grant. So the committed order produces the permission-shaped artifact, while the window still admits at most one grant per term. I kept the judgement carefully scoped: recorded as 'a grant that skips the freshness check is producible under a stop between the two writes', explicitly not 'a committed entry is lost', with the severity left conditional on the vote split and on the intersection between any quorum and the nodes holding the committed entries, and with the earlier unresolved interpretation and its counterevidence preserved alongside.
